Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:10:1.english: Where he found it in a garbage dump - For it is the way of a carcass to be thrown into a garbage dump.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:11:2.english: [He] found skeins with which weavers weave - He found balls of spun [thread] for traps and nets in a place where hunters are commonly found.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:12:1.english: One found produce inside a vessel - And an ordinary vessel has a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:12:3.english: A pouch - It has an identifying mark for the owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:12:4.hebrew: צבורי פירות - בגמ' מפרש סימנייהו, או מנין או מקום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:12:4.english: Piles of produce - In the Gemara, it explains their identifying marks: either number or location.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:1:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא לעולם רבנן - ובשאינה טמון, ולא תפשוט מינה דמודו ליה ברוב כנענים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:1:1.english: And if you wish, say [that] actually [it is] the Rabbis - And [it refers to a case] where [the item] is not concealed, and do not resolve from it that they agree with him [regarding a city with] a majority of Canaanites.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:1:2.hebrew: מי קתני כו' אינו חייב להכריז קתני - דכיון דרובא כנענים, דלמא דכנענים הוא, ושלו נמי לא הויא, דלא אזלי רבנן בתר רובא בממונא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:1:2.english: Is it taught, etc., "he is not obligated to proclaim" is taught - For since the majority are Canaanites [i.e., gentiles], perhaps it belongs to Canaanites; and it is not his either, for the Rabbis do not follow the majority in monetary matters.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:2:1.english: [It is] permitted in terms of finding [lost items] - For he is not obligated to proclaim [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:2:2.hebrew: ואסורה בהנאה - ולקמיה פריך, א"כ, מה היתר יש במציאתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:2:2.english: And [it] is prohibited for benefit - And later [the Gemara] asks: If so, what permissibility is there in finding it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:2:3.hebrew: בא ישראל ונתן סימן - יצאת מספק יין כנענים, ומותרת בשתיה למוצאה, דכיון דרובא כנענים, נתייאשו הבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:2:3.english: A Jew came and gave a distinguishing mark - It is removed from the doubt of gentile wine and is permitted for drinking to its finder, for since the majority are gentiles, the owners despaired [of recovering it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:1.english: And cast into the Biran River - And [they were] thrown into the Biran River.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:2.hebrew: דמתקיל - יש בו מכשולים — אבנים וסתימת גדר שעושין לדגים — ולא מיאש. סבר: לא יוכל הנהר להוליכם חוץ למכשולים, ורגילים היו לסוכרו ולנקותו ולכרותו שישטפו מימיו, וסומך שימצאם כשיסכרו אותו וינקום:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:2.english: That it contains obstacles - It has obstacles — stones and a fence-dam that they make for fish — and [the owner] does not despair. He thinks [to himself]: the river will not be able to carry them past the obstacles; and they were accustomed to dam it, clean it, and dredge it so that its waters would flow away, and he relies [on the expectation] that he will find them when they dam it and clean them out.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:3.hebrew: סכרו ליה - שקורין נשנ"ש בלע"ז, כמו עושי שכר אגמי נפש (ישעיהו יט):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:3.english: They dammed it - [With] what is called nasses [weirs/dams] in the vernacular [Old French], as [in the verse], "who make dams [sekher], ponds of water" (Isaiah 19[:10]).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:4.hebrew: אימא מישראל נפיל - לפיכך חייב להכריז, ולא אמרינן יניח, כדאמרינן לעיל ברוב כנענים לרבנן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:4.english: Say [that] it fell from a Jew - Therefore, he is obligated to proclaim [the find], and we do not say [that] he should leave [it aside], as we said above regarding a majority of gentiles according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:5:5.english: He does not despair - For the dredger will find them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:6:1.hebrew: דבי דיסא - שמוכרים שם חטים כתושין לדייסא, ורבים מצויין שם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:6:1.english: Of the place of pounded grain - Where they sell crushed wheat for pounded-grain porridge, and many [people] are found there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:6:2.english: After twelve months of the year - [that is when] he found them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:8:1.hebrew: דיו - עוף שקורין אוזלטו"ר, והוא לשון דיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:8:1.english: Dayo [a kite] - A bird that is called ozeltor [in Old French], and it is a form of [the word] dayah [kite].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:8:2.english: And cast it among the palm trees of the house of Bar Maryon - It threw it among the palm trees of Bar Maryon.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:8:3.english: Forbidden - Lest it was exchanged for [meat of] an unslaughtered carcass.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 24b:8:4.english: And sees it - From when [the kite] took it until it cast it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:10:1.hebrew: שמצאן באשפה - בפ"ק דחולין (ד' יב:) מפרש: נראין דברי רבי יהודה לרבי חנניא כשמצאן באשפה שבשוק, שאף רבי חנניא לא פליג עליה אלא באשפה שבבית; ובעובדא דהכא שמצאן בדרך בלא אשפה, הוי כאשפה שבבית:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:10:1.english: "Where he found them in a garbage dump" - In the first chapter of Chullin (12b), [the Gemara] explains: The words of Rabbi Yehuda appear [correct] to Rabbi Chananya when he found them in a garbage dump in the marketplace, for even Rabbi Chananya only disagreed with him regarding a garbage dump in a house; and in the incident here, where he found them on the road without a garbage dump, it is like [finding them in] a garbage dump in a house.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:11:1.hebrew: אתא לקמיה דרבי אסי - גרסי'. אע"ג דבכל דוכתי חשיב רבי אמי ברישא, כדאמר (גיטין דף נט:): "רבי אמי ורבי אסי כהני חשיבי דארעא דישראל", אף על גב שגדול ממנו — אין תימה שבא לפניו לישאל, לפי שחבירו היה. אבל אי גרסינן "רבי אבא" — קשה; דרבי אבא היה תלמידו של רבי אמי, כדמוכח גבי נסכא דרבי אבא (שבועות דף מז.), ואיך היה בא לפניו (לעולם):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:11:1.english: He came before Rabbi Asi - This is our reading. Even though in all places Rabbi Ami is listed first — as it says (Gittin 59b): "Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, the prominent priests of the Land of Israel" — [and] even though [Rabbi Ami] was greater than him, it is not surprising that he came before him to inquire, because he was his colleague. However, if we read "Rabbi Abba," it is difficult: for Rabbi Abba was a student of Rabbi Ami, as is evident regarding the [silver] ingot of Rabbi Abba (Shevuot 47a), so how could [Rabbi Ami] have come before him (ever)?

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:3:1.hebrew: סבר כוותיה בחדא - ולא בעי למימר דסבר כרבנן, דא"כ תפשוט דמודו רבנן ברוב כנענים; ומכל מקום יש לפשוט דהלכה כמותו ברוב כנענים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:3:1.english: He holds in accordance with him in one [case] - And [the Gemara] does not wish to say that he [Rav Asi] holds like the Rabbis, for if so, you could resolve [the question] that the Rabbis concede in [a place with] a majority of Canaanites [gentiles]; nevertheless, one can resolve that the halakha is in accordance with him in [a place with] a majority of Canaanites.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:6:1.hebrew: לבתר תריסר ירחי שתא כו' - פי': הן עצמן החזיר, אע"ג דלא היה צריך ליתן רק דמיהם, כדתנן בפרקין (דף כח:): "כל דבר שעושה ואוכל — מטפל בו י"ב חדש; מכאן ואילך — שם דמיהן ומניחן". אבל רש"י פירש שמצאן אחר י"ב חדש שנאבדו — קשה: דמנלן שיהא בשביל כך למוצא? דהאובד אינו מתיאש, שסבור שהמוצא יסבור שמקרוב נאבדו, ויכריז:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:6:1.english: "After twelve months of the year, etc." - Explanation: He returned [the donkeys] themselves, even though he was only required to give their value, as we learned in the Mishnah in our chapter (28b): "Anything that works and eats — one cares for it for twelve months; from then on, he assesses its value and sets it aside." However, Rashi explained that he found them twelve months after they were lost — [this is] difficult: for how do we know that because of this it belongs to the finder? For the one who lost [it] does not despair, since he thinks that the finder will assume it was lost recently and will proclaim [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:6:2.hebrew: לפנים משורת הדין - מ"אשר יעשון" נפקא לן לקמן בפרקין (בבא מציעא דף ל:). תימה, דלא מייתי קרא הכא כדמייתי לקמן בעובדא דר' ישמעאל ובהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף ק. ושם ד"ה לפנים) בעובדא דרבי חייא במראה דינר לשולחני ונמצא רע, ולקמן בסוף פרק האומנין (בבא מציעא דף פג.) מייתי קרא אחרינא: "למען תלך בדרך טובים", שהוא מדברי קבלה, ושביק קרא ד"אשר יעשון", שהוא מדברי תורה. וי"ל, דלא מייתי קרא ד"אשר יעשון" אלא במקום שאחרים חייבין והוא פטור — כמו במראה דינר, דאחרים דבעו למילף חייבים, ור' חייא דלא בעי למילף פטור, ולפנים משורת הדין שילם כמו אחרים; וכן בעובדא דרבי ישמעאל, דזקן ואינו לפי כבודו הוה, ועשה לפנים משורת הדין כמו אחרים. והכא בשמעתין, דהדרינהו בתר תריסר ירחי שתא, כ"ע פטורים; לכך לא מייתי קרא הכא, ומ"מ משום לפנים משורת הדין בעי ליה לאהדורי, כיון שאינו מתחסר ממונא. אבל בסוף האומנין (שם), בהנהו שקולאי ששברו לו החבית ועשו לו הפסד גדול, משום לפנים משורת הדין אין לו להפסיד; לכך מייתי קרא "למען תלך בדרך טובים":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:6:2.english: Beyond the letter of the law - This is derived from [the verse] "which they must do" [Exodus 18:20] later in our chapter (Bava Metzia 30b). It is puzzling why [the Gemara] does not cite that verse here, as it cites it later in the incident of Rabbi Yishmael, and in [chapter] HaGozel Kamma (Bava Kamma 100a, and there, s.v. Lifnim) in the incident of Rabbi Chiya regarding one who shows a dinar to a moneychanger and it turns out to be bad; and later at the end of [chapter] HaOmanin (Bava Metzia 83a), it cites a different verse: "So that you may walk in the way of the good" [Proverbs 2:20], which is from the words of Tradition [i.e., the Writings], and leaves aside the verse "which they must do," which is from the words of the Torah. And one can answer that [the Gemara] only cites the verse "which they must do" in a case where others are obligated and he is exempt — such as in [the case of] showing a dinar, where others who need to learn [the craft] are obligated, while Rabbi Chiya, who did not need to learn, was exempt, yet beyond the letter of the law he paid like others; and similarly in the incident of Rabbi Yishmael, where he was an elder and it was not in keeping with his dignity, yet he acted beyond the letter of the law like others. Here in our sugya, however, where he returned [the donkeys] after twelve months of the year, everyone is exempt; therefore [the Gemara] does not cite the verse here, and nevertheless, on account of [acting] beyond the letter of the law, he ought to return [them], since he does not suffer a monetary loss. But at the end of HaOmanin (ibid.), regarding those porters who broke his barrel and caused him a great loss, one does not have to suffer a loss on account of [acting] beyond the letter of the law; therefore [the Gemara] cites the verse "So that you may walk in the way of the good."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:8:1.hebrew: אתא לקמיה דרב - גרסי' כדמשמע בירושלמי פרק אין מעמידין. ואפילו לספרים דגרסי אביי, פריך שפיר מבשר שנתעלם מן העין; דאף ע"ג דלא קיימא לן כרב, כדפרישית לעיל (בבא מציעא דף כג: ד"ה מחרוזות), מדפריך בפרק גיד הנשה (חולין דף צה: ושם) "ורב היכי אכיל בשרא?", מ"מ פריך שפיר, דכיון דחזי המוצא שהעוף השליכם שם, אפילו מאן דפליג ארב מודה הכא דאסור, דאימור נטלה מעיר שרובה כנענים. ומשני: בעומד ורואהו שנטלה מעיר שרובה טבחי ישראל. ולרב מיירי בעומד ורואה שנטלה לפני טבחי ישראל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:8:1.english: [He] came before Rav - We read [the text as "Rav"], as is implied in the Jerusalem Talmud, [in] the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin. And even according to the editions that read "Abaye," [the Gemara] asks well from [the ruling regarding] meat that was obscured from sight; for even though the law is not in accordance with Rav — as I explained above (Bava Metzia 23b, s.v. Macharozot), from the fact that [the Gemara] asks in the chapter [entitled] Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 95b and there), "And how did Rav eat meat?" — nevertheless, [the Gemara] asks well [here]. For since the finder saw that the bird cast it there, even the one who disagrees with Rav concedes here that it is forbidden, for one can say [the bird] took it from a city whose majority is non-Jews. And [the Gemara] answers: [It refers to a case] where he stands and sees it, that [the bird] took it from a city whose majority is Jewish butchers. And according to [the reading] "Rav," [the Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where he stands and sees that [the bird] took it in front of Jewish butchers.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:9:1.hebrew: הרי שאבדו כו' - ה"ה נגנבו, ואע"ג דעבר על "לא תגנוב", לא עבר על לאו דנבילה. ובתוספתא (פ"ב דחולין) תניא בהדיא: "הרי שאבדו או נגנבו", והכא נקט "אבדו" אורחא דמילתא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 24b:9:1.english: "Where [they] were lost, etc." - The same applies [if] they were stolen, and even though [the thief] transgressed "You shall not steal," he did not transgress the negative commandment of nevelah. And in the Tosefta (Chullin, ch. 2) it is explicitly taught: "Where they were lost or stolen," and here [the baraita] stated "were lost" [simply as] the usual case.
